questions.q: What were the names of Zelophehad’s five daughters?
questions.a: Zelophehad’s five daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

questions.q: Where did Zelophehad’s daughters stand when they made their request?
questions.a: They stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, in front of Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole community.

questions.q: Why did Zelophehad die in the wilderness?
questions.a: Zelophehad died in the wilderness, not because he was one of those who gathered against Yahweh in the company of Korah, but because of his own sin.

questions.q: What did the daughters of Zelophehad want Moses to give them?
questions.a: The daughters of Zelophehad wanted Moses to give them land among their father’s relatives.

questions.q: What did Moses do with the daughters’ request?
questions.a: Moses brought their request before Yahweh and asked him what to do.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses about the daughters’ request?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses that the daughters were right and that he must give them the land their father would have received.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say should happen to the inheritance of a man when he dies and has no son?
questions.a: When a man dies without a son, his inheritance must pass to his daughter.

questions.q: If a man has no son or daughter, who receives his inheritance next?
questions.a: If a man has no son or daughter, his inheritance passes to his brothers.

questions.q: If a man has no brothers, who receives his inheritance?
questions.a: If a man has no brothers, his inheritance passes to his father’s brothers.

questions.q: If a man has no uncles, who receives his inheritance?
questions.a: If a man has no uncles, his nearest relative in his clan receives his inheritance.

questions.q: Why was Moses to be gathered with his people instead of going into the land which Yahweh had given them?
questions.a: Moses was to be gathered with his people because he and Aaron disobeyed Yahweh in the wilderness of Zin, when they did not show the Israelites that Yahweh is holy while giving them water.

questions.q: Why did Moses ask Yahweh to appoint a man over the community?
questions.a: Moses asked that Yahweh appoint a man over the community so they would not be like sheep that have no shepherd.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh instruct Moses to lay his hand on Joshua, son of Nun?
questions.a: Yahweh instructed Moses to choose Joshua because he was a man in whom Yahweh’s spirit lived.

questions.q: How much of his authority did Yahweh command Moses to give to Joshua?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded Moses to give Joshua some of his own authority, so that the whole Israelite community would obey Joshua.

questions.q: How did Moses respond to Yahweh’s command?
questions.a: Moses did as Yahweh had instructed: he placed Joshua before Eleazar the priest and the whole community, laid his hands on him, and commissioned him to lead.

commentary.text: The daughters of Zelophehad apply for an inheritance, The law of inheritances.

Verses 1–11 The five daughters of Zelophehad considered themselves as left destitute, having neither father nor brother to inherit any land. Their believing expectation that the word of the Lord would be performed in due season, and their desire of an interest in the promised inheritance; and the modest, candid manner in which they asked, without secret murmurs or discontents, are a good example. They ask for a possession in the land of Canaan. Herein they discovered, 1. Strong faith in the power and promise of God, concerning the giving of the land of Canaan to Israel. 2. And earnest desire of a place and name in the land of promise, which was a type of heaven. 3. Respect and honour for their father, whose name was dear to them now he was gone. He never had done any thing that might bar his children's claim. It is a comfort to parents when they come to die, if though they have smarted for their own sin, yet they are not conscious of any of those iniquities which God will visit on their children. God himself gives judgment. He takes notice of the affairs, not only of nations, but of private families, and orders them according to his will. The petition is granted. Those who seek an inheritance in the land of promise, shall have what they seek for, and other things shall be added to them.

Moses must die, but he shall have the satisfaction of seeing the land of promise. This sight of Canaan signified his believing prospect of the better country, that is, the heavenly. Moses must die, but death does not cut him off; it only brings him to rest with the holy patriarchs. It is but to die as they died, having lived as they lived; and as their end was peace, why should we fear any evil in the passage of that dark valley? (Nu 27:15-23)

Envious spirits do not love their successors; but Moses was not one of these. We should concern ourselves, both in our prayers and in our endeavours, for the rising generation, that religion may be maintained and advanced, when we are in our graves. God appoints a successor, even Joshua; who had signalized himself by his courage in fighting Amalek, his humility in ministering to Moses, and his faith and sincerity in witnessing against the report of the evil spies. This man God appoints to succeed Moses; a man in whom is the Spirit, the Spirit of grace. He is a good man, fearing God and hating covetousness, and acting from principle. He has the spirit of government; he is fit to do the work and discharge the trusts of his place. He has a spirit of conduct and courage; he had also the Spirit of prophecy. That man is not fully qualified for any service in the church of Christ, who is destitute of the graces and gifts of the Holy Spirit, whatever human abilities he may possess. And in Joshua's succession we are reminded “that the law was given by Moses,” who by reason of our transgression could not bring us to heaven; but “grace and truth came by Jesus Christ,” for the salvation of every believer.
